title: The advisory hook keeps its own extension-to-language map beside the binary's lang_of
body:
## What

`lib/templates/.claude/scripts/post-tool-advisory.sh:68-75` decides which critic runs on an edited file from a `case` on the file's extension: `.ex` and `.exs` are elixir, `.rs` rust, `.swift` swift, `.lua` lua, `.sh`, `.bash` and `.zsh` shell, and anything else exits 0 with no critic run. The binary already has the one map, `lang_of` in `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/index/corpus.rs:109`, which the index and search read.

The two agree today. A language added to `lang_of`, or a new extension for an existing language, is skipped by the hook without a word, because its `*) exit 0` arm cannot tell an extension nobody handles from one it was never told about.

## Expected

The hook takes a file's language from the binary instead of from its own table: `intent critic` derives it from `lang_of` for the path it is given (or a read verb answers it), so a file's language is decided in one place.

Found by cc's sweep for second copies of the binary's project checks, on hv's question of 2026-10-22. No lane yet.

## Spec (vc, 2026-10-23, ruling on ic's surface note, blob 13571783fc26)

LANE: cc builds. SHAPE: `intent lang of <path>`, in the `lang` family beside `lang show`: one path, arity 1; no project needed, so it answers anywhere as `lang list` does; no existence check, since the hook tests `-f` itself; reads `lang_of` (index/corpus.rs:109, whose names are `critic::HEADLESS_LANGUAGES`, pinned by a test); prints the language on one line at rc 0, or nothing at rc 0 when the extension maps to none, which is then the authoritative "no critic for this file" that the hook's `*) exit 0` arm could never say; a missing argument is clap's usage error, rc 1. `intent critic` is NOT made to derive a language from a path: its positional picks the pack, each rule matches by its own `applies_to` globs (corpus.rs:96-106), and its exit codes are load-bearing for the gate (0 clean, 1 findings, 2 usage, 3 refused). CONSUMER, in the templates bank: post-tool-advisory.sh:68-75's `case` table becomes `lang="$(intent lang of "$file_path")"; [ -n "$lang" ] || exit 0`, after the `command -v intent` test moved above it, then the same `intent critic "$lang" --files ...` call. PROOF: CLI arms: `foo.rs` prints rust, `foo.ex` elixir, `foo.txt` nothing at rc 0, no argument rc 1; and the hook's bats arm drives the advisory with a planted file and asserts the table is gone and the verb is called (the two maps agree today, so the red control is structural). ORDER and CLOSE: as 0618's; the three close together on the templates landing.
